इस पावन यात्रा में मेरे साथ जाने-माने ज्योतिषाचार्य और मेरे गुरु समान डॉ. अरविंद द्विवेदी जी, मेरे बड़े भाई कँवल सिक्का जी और मेरे बचपन के दोस्त विजय शर्मा जी भी मौजूद रहे, जिनकी उपस्थिति ने इस यात्रा को और भी विशेष और यादगार बना दिया। बाबा बैद्यनाथ के दर्शन और रुद्राभिषेक कर मन को अद्भुत शांति और आध्यात्मिक ऊर्जा का अनुभव हुआ। 

इसके बाद कालभैरव मंदिर में बाबा भैरव के दर्शन कर आशीर्वाद प्राप्त किया और फिर आखिर में बासुकीनाथ मंदिर में भगवान शिव के नाग स्वरूप के दर्शन कर यह आध्यात्मिक यात्रा पूर्ण हुई।

इस संपूर्ण यात्रा ने मन को गहरी शांति, आत्मा को संतोष और मस्तिष्क को नई ऊर्जा व मजबूती प्रदान की।

snippet.title: The Death of State Fairs: What Really Went Wrong
snippet.description:
Once a symbol of American community, fried food, and summer nostalgia — state fairs are now collapsing. Rising insurance costs, vendor bankruptcies, and declining attendance are forcing many fairs to downsize or shut down completely. This video uncovers what really went wrong with state fairs — and why they may never recover.

We’ll look at how these once-beloved events became too expensive to run, how safety concerns and corporate control changed their culture, and why the small-town charm that made them special is disappearing. From family-run food stands closing to fairs being priced out by modern entertainment, this is the untold story of the state fair’s downfall.

If you grew up going to state fairs — or wondered why they don’t feel the same anymore — this video breaks down the real reasons behind their decline.

snippet.title: Strike on Iran: The Nuclear Question (updated documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
An investigation into the status of Iran’s nuclear program amid the second round of U.S.-Israeli military action in less than a year. (March 2026 update)

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

In the weeks since the U.S. and Israel began bombarding Iran, President Trump has repeatedly justified the strikes by claiming Iran had posed an imminent nuclear threat. But nine months earlier, in the wake of U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran in June 2025, the message coming from Washington was that Iran’s key nuclear facilities had been “obliterated.”

Drawing on new reporting, satellite imagery analysis and interviews, this investigation is an updated presentation of our December 2025 documentary by the same name.

In September of last year, directors Adam Desiderio and Sebastian Walker, who is also the film’s correspondent, visited sites hit in the June 2025 U.S.-Israeli strikes and sat down with one of Iran’s most powerful officials, Ali Larijani — in what turned out to be the last on-camera interview he gave to an American news outlet before his assassination earlier this month in an Israeli airstrike. 

Since the current war began, the team has been talking to experts and officials and analyzing satellite imagery with The Washington Post, Bellingcat and Evident Media to try to understand the truth about what remains of Iran’s nuclear program.

Their findings offer valuable insights into a continuing conflict that has rippled across the Middle East, killing thousands — including children at an elementary school — and displacing millions.

“Strike on Iran” is a FRONTLINE production with Mongoose Pictures in association with The ‪@WashingtonPost‬ ‪@evidentmedia‬ and ‪@bellingcatofficial‬. It is written, produced and directed by Adam Desiderio and Sebastian Walker. The correspondent is Sebastian Walker. The reporters are Nilo Tabrizy, Jarrett Ley, Souad Mekhennet, Trevor Ball, Carlos Gonzales and Sebastian Vandermeersch. The senior producers are Dan Edge and Eamonn Matthews. The editor-in-chief and executive producer of FRONTLINE is Raney Aronson-Rath.

In the world of Indian Startups, Dunzo was the pioneer. Long before Swiggy Instamart, Zepto, or Blinkit existed, Dunzo was "digitizing the offline world." But as this case study reveals, being a first-mover is often a curse.

This strategy severely slowed German troops, cut off their fuel and food supplies, and weakened their morale. By the time they reached Stalingrad, German soldiers were exhausted, starving, and unprepared for the brutal Russian winter. This devastating plan became one of the biggest turning points of World War 2 and played a crucial role in Nazi Germany’s defeat.

K. R. Nagarajan started his career as a sales representative in a Khadi store in 1977, where he noticed that dhoti weavers earned very little money and received almost no respect.

To change this, he launched Ramraj Cotton in 1983, giving weavers better salaries, food, and living facilities.

But the real turning point came after a humiliating incident.

One day, Nagarajan went to a five-star hotel with business colleagues — but was stopped at the entrance simply because he was wearing a dhoti.

That insult made him realize one thing:
People didn’t see dhoti as modern, premium, or respectable anymore.

So instead of changing himself, he changed society’s perception.

Ramraj launched powerful marketing campaigns where industrialists, celebrities, and influential people proudly wore dhotis and were treated with admiration and respect.

Slowly, dhoti transformed from a “traditional outfit” into a symbol of status and pride.

Today, Ramraj Cotton sells over 2,500 varieties of dhotis worldwide and has built a ₹2,000 crore empire — all from one insult that changed everything.

snippet.title: How North Korea Created Record of Biggest Hotel
snippet.description:
How North Korea Created Record of Biggest Hotel  ! Aman Sharma
In 1986, after seeing South Korea build the world’s tallest hotel, North Korean dictator Kim Il-sung decided to build an even bigger one — the massive Ryugyong Hotel.

With 105 floors, 3,000 rooms, and revolving restaurants, it was supposed to become a symbol of North Korea’s power. But in 1992, the country’s economy collapsed and construction stopped completely.

What remained was a giant unfinished concrete pyramid ruining the skyline of Pyongyang. No windows, no paint, no opening.

To hide this embarrassment, North Korea reportedly removed the hotel from maps and official photos for years — pretending it never existed.

Later, they covered it with glass panels and LED lights just to make it look modern from the outside. But the shocking truth is that even after nearly 40 years, the hotel has still never officially opened.

Today, its LED screens mostly display government propaganda instead of guests.
